question: Does a learned choice of which violated not-all-equal knot to attend to next and which of its distinctions to flip, with memory of earlier steps, reduce work per instance below tuned hand-written local rules on planted knot patterns where exact search is costly, and does it carry over to unseen and larger instances and to a second meeting pattern?
inputs: The agent's local reads: break and make of the attended knot's distinctions; for each where-candidate (up to three knots just violated by its last flip and three drawn uniformly from the violated ones) its least, mean and zero-count break, whether it was just violated and whether it overlaps the knot just acted on; with memory, visit and flip ages, ranks, recent counts and a recurrent state.
forbidden_inputs: The hidden planted state, the global violated count beyond the recurrent input's log count, any test instance during training or tuning, and any solver output.
mapping: Softmax policy over candidates from two 8-unit scorers and a 6-unit recurrent state (326 weights), trained by OpenAI-ES on a curriculum of rand training instances n = 200, 400, 800; frozen for testing.
primary_observable: R = median flips of L3 / median flips of the best re-tuned hand-written rule on unseen rand n = 3200 instances, with a paired bootstrap interval; marginal CPU and incidences per instance and break-even N*.
comparators_or_controls: Random agent; WalkSAT, probSAT, Novelty+, greedy-where, sticky (follow what you broke) and focused Metropolis, each tuned on training instances and re-tuned per test cell; CaDiCaL as exact-search context; learned ablations L1 (no where, no memory), L2w (learned where, fixed probSAT what), L2 (no memory).
resource_budget: Eight ES trainings (about 12 CPU-hours) and test cells to rand n = 12800 and local n = 3200, CPU only, MemoryMax 16G under the shared runner.
first_executable_signal: Gate G: every reported solution satisfies every knot, incremental counts match recomputation, zero weights act uniformly, a break-preferring mutant is slower, CaDiCaL models check; then G-learn: L1 within 1.15 times probSAT at training size.
stop_rule: Stop at the frozen decision rule (real win, mechanism win, clean loss, inconclusive, or learner failure if G-learn fails); keep every run, failed or censored.
nonclaims: Planted instances only; no general SAT method; no claim about unrestricted solvers, P vs NP, native emergence or self-improving AI; the knot structures are fixed and their change (the second stage) is not tested.
